definitions.gloss: visiting a store; coming to a shop (honorific)
definitions.explanation: Honorific form used by shop staff addressing customers.

examples.japanese: ご{来店|らいてん}ありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you for visiting our store.

examples.japanese: ご{来店|らいてん}の{際|さい}は、ご{予約|よやく}をお{願|ねが}いいたします。
examples.english: Please make a reservation when you visit.

examples.japanese: {本日|ほんじつ}もご{来店|らいてん}いただき、{誠|まこと}にありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you very much for visiting us today as well.

examples.japanese: ご{来店|らいてん}いただいたお{客様|きゃくさま}{全員|ぜんいん}にプレゼントを{差|さ}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.english: We will give a gift to every customer who visits.

notes:
The honorific prefix ご + {来店|らいてん} (visiting a store). This is standard keigo used by service staff to politely refer to a customer's visit. You will hear this phrase in virtually every retail and restaurant environment in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ご{来店|らいてん}ありがとうございます: thank you for visiting
- ご{来店|らいてん}をお{待|ま}ちしております: we look forward to your visit
- ご{来店|らいてん}の{際|さい}: when you visit
- ご{来店|らいてん}いただく: to have someone visit (humble/honorific)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ご{来場|らいじょう}: visiting a venue (events, exhibitions)
- ご{来院|らいいん}: visiting a hospital or clinic
- ご{来社|らいしゃ}: visiting a company office
- ご{来館|らいかん}: visiting a public facility (library, museum)
